newsitem.title: THAILAND: Foreigners dump Thai bank stocks for baht funds.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners dump Thai bank stocks for baht funds.

text.p: Foreign investors dumped bank stocks on the foreign board of the Thai stock exchange for the second day on Tuesday, apparently to raise baht funds, brokers said.
Major Thai banks tumbled on the foreign board with Bangkok Bank losing 15 baht to 175, Thai Farmers Bank retreating 6.50 to 98.50, and Siam Commercial Bank declining 2.50 to 97.00.
On the bourse's main board, the banking counter also led the market retreat, losing 3.61 percent at 0510 GMT against a 2.18 percent decline for the overall market.

Brokers said traditional hefty price premiums fetched by major banks on the foreign board have fallen sharply during the past few sessions, apparently due to a need by foreign fund managers to raise baht funds to cover baht/dollar positions.
On the main board, Bangkok Bank lost six baht to 126, Thai Farmers shed 3.50 to 86.00, and Siam Commercial Bank fell 2.50 to 95.50.

The Thai baht has been in short supply in offshore markets since mid-May after the Bank of Thailand blocked access for foreign speculators trying to raise baht funds needed for betting against the currency.
Bangkok Bank has tumbled on the foreign board during the past two months, to 176 baht at the Tuesday lunch break from its 212 baht close last Thursday and 278 on April 17.
The baht was quoted offshore at 23.400/500 to the dollar during midday Tuesday, substantially higher than about 25.800 traded in the domestic market.
Brokers said Thai banks have also been squeezed recently by expected declining profitability and weak second quarter earnings.
